articles.title: John Romero's Next Shooter Survived the Microsoft Purge, Now He's Taking Inspiration From The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
articles.summary: John Romero, the legendary game designer who co-founded id Software has had a career spanning five decades. During that time he’s enjoyed the highest of highs, such as his seminal work on Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, and Quake, and the lowest of lows, most recently when his current studio Romero Games had…
body: Speaking with IGN during Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 this week, where he delivered an opening keynote address titled, ‘Why We Still Make Games,’ Romero seemed upbeat about the direction of his latest project despite 2025’s devastating setback. In fact, almost a year on from the loss in funding and the resulting reduction of his studio from 110 members of staff down to just five, Romero claimed that he was “doing better than [he’d] done in decades.”

“It really sucked,” said Romero of the brutal blindsiding by Microsoft in 2025. “[But] I don't have bitterness because that's not who I am, really. I always move forward. So it's like, that happened. Now we have to figure out where to go from here.”

While Romero remained tight-lipped on the specifics, he was happy to confirm that Romero Games’ latest project has secured a new publishing partner and that development is proceeding well despite the substantial reduction in resources at the studio.

articles.title: Capcom Isn't Scrapping Resident Evil, but Mainline Story Could Wrap Up in Next 10 Years According to Producer
articles.summary: IGN recently reported that Resident Evil series producer Jun Takeuchi commented that Capcom’s survival horror series’ story could end in the next 10 years. However, this does not mean that Capcom plans to stop making Resident Evil games in the next decade.
body: As Takeuchi told 47 News (picked up by Yahoo Japan ) in a recent interview, “With the release of Requiem this year, I feel like the first 10 years have reached the end of a chapter, so I think the conclusion will come in the following 10 years."

This quote set news outlets and fans wondering if Capcom plans to wind up its popular franchise by 2036. However, what Takeuchi is specifically referring to here is the company’s 10-year branding concept for the survival horror franchise. This vision kicked off with the 2019 remake of Resident Evil 2, which Takeuchi refers to in the previous paragraph, and involved much mulling over how to deal with Resident Evil’s overarching story.

“The series' story wasn't all planned out from the beginning, it expanded with each new release," Takeuchi said. "When we were planning the Resident Evil 2 remake and coming up with the 10-year branding concept, this (the story) was what we puzzled over. If you play through all of these games, I think you'll work out the meaning behind the order of the remakes.”
points: IGN recently reported that Resident Evil series producer Jun Takeuchi commented that Capcom’s survival horror series’ story could end in the next 10 years.
However, this does not mean that Capcom plans to stop making Resident Evil games in the next decade.

articles.title: Celeste and TowerFall dev explains why both games were suddenly delisted from Xbox
articles.summary: Celeste and TowerFall have both been delisted from Xbox suddenly earlier this week. Per a post on Bluesky, developer Maddy Thorson says this was an intentional move, with the games being removed from sale on Xbox in support of the BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement, which is aimed at…
body: "For those who're asking, yes we delisted Celeste and TowerFall on Xbox," states Thorson in a BlueSky post. "We did this to support the BDS boycott."

In case you're unaware, Xbox's inclusion on the BDS list is due to Microsoft's partnership with Israel and its prison system, according to BDS itself. The company has provided the country use of its Azure Cloud and AI systems, which have been used consistently over the past few years in the ongoing subjugation of Palestinians. BDS has urged people to cancel their Game Pass subscriptions, boycott leading Xbox franchises - including Call of Duty and Candy Crush - and cease purchases of Microsoft gaming products. As it stands, Celeste and TowerFall are now completely unavailable for purchase within the Xbox ecosystem.

This isn't the first time we've seen developers intentionally opt out of sales on Xbox because of the BDS movement; just a few weeks ago, Big Walk developer House House released a statement noting that its game is not on Xbox because of Microsoft's ties to Israel, and we saw the developer of Tenderfoot Tactics do the same in 2025.
points: Celeste and TowerFall have both been delisted from Xbox suddenly earlier this week.

articles.title: 10 Queer Fairy Tale Retellings Better Than the Originals
articles.summary: As a queer woman growing up, it was pretty easy to neg on all things fairy-tale. Perhaps I had reason to, as mockery of all things Disney has grown popular in recent years.
body: The truth, though, was that no matter how eye-rollingly saccharine and over-the-top fairy tales were, my biggest criticism was that I couldn’t see myself or people like me in their pages or on my television screen. That bitterness put me off fairy tales right up until I discovered a pivotal genre: queer fairy-tale retellings.

Queer retellings have grown increasingly popular over the years. The breadth of mythological tales gives authors room to add their own spin, transforming old heteronormative stories into something fresh and exciting.
To celebrate Adult Fairy Tales Week, we’ve rounded up the best queer fairy-tale reads — from young adult romance to spine-chilling horror — that you owe it to yourself to read at least once.

Sexton’s short novella that reimagines the classic tale, staying true to the original while adding a fun, gay twist. Eldon Cinder wants only to see his friend, Prince Xavier, one last time at the royal ball. But only women are invited to dance with the prince. So Eldon visits a local witch, who grants his wish — with a huge catch.

articles.summary: Hideo Kojima's Death Stranding series brought the Metal Gear Solid creator's trademark arthouse approach to video games to full fruition. With no plans for Death Stranding 3, besides a concept draft, fans are instead looking forward to the game's universe expanding into different media, including…
body: Death Stranding Isolations was announced in 2025. This original net anime will be a new story with different protagonists from Death Stranding and Death Stranding 2: On the Beach. The first trailer, released on Oct. 30, shows one of the two main characters, a girl with blonde hair. She is tormented by visions of Beached Things (BTs), the souls of the dead that are stranded in the world of the living. The anime's subtitle is "My mom became a crater," a reference to the voidouts, the massive explosions triggered when a BT consumes a human.

Death Stranding Isolations will be animated by E&H Production, a relatively new animation studio founded by MAPPA veteran Sunghoo Park, whose credits include Ninja Kamui and the upcoming Magic Knight Rayearth remake. Isolations will be directed by Takyuki Sano ( Attack on Titan: The Last Attack, Jujutsu Kaisen 0 ), an industry veteran making his directorial debut. The screenplay comes from Tow Ubukata, an award-winning novelist and screenwriter famous for Psycho-Pass 2 and 3.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
articles.summary: Beloved actor Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. The veteran of stage and screen was best known for his many years as Star Trek's Jean-Luc Picard and X-Men's Charles Xavier, though he also had notable roles in video games, including The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and Castlevania: Lords of…
body: "We announce with grew sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dimentia" a statement on his official Instagram reads. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace."

Stewart's role as Picard made him a household name, and following the conclusion of Star Trek: The Next Generation, he reprised the role in several Star Trek films as well as the series Star Trek: Picard.

articles.title: 5 Classic JRPGs with Virtually Perfect Battle Systems
articles.summary: Many role-playing games have a familiar, turn-based combat system. Your options are usually riffs on one of four actions: attack, defend, use magic, or use an item. Even with that very basic template, you’re usually in for a pretty fun time saving the world with a group of pals.
body: A rare few RPGs manage to elevate this simple format into an experience worth savoring over the course of dozens of hours. Below, you’ll find five such games. Some of these JRPG battle systems have stood the test of time because they’re remarkably well-balanced, while others are just a ton of fun to break. Either way, they’re keeping players coming back year after year for good reason.

Getting a job has never been more fun than in Final Fantasy Tactics. There are 33 different jobs in Square Enix’s grid-based strategy RPG, and any character is free to become a master in any one of them. (Pretty much, anyway.) Want to be a white mage who’s also handy with an axe? Or a swordsman with an arsenal of spells that speed up and slow down time? You can have those kind of oddball combinations in Final Fantasy Tactics. Heck, you can do that with the same character from one battle to the next.

But with all that fluidity comes the expectation that you’ll use it to your advantage in any given situation. Fights are punishingly tough, and you’ll need to bring a precisely built squad into every plot-relevant fight, even in the slightly gentler Ivalice Chronicles remake that came out last year.

Your options are usually riffs on one of four actions: attack, defend, use magic, or use an item.

articles.title: 34 Years Later, Hobbes' Wisest 'Calvin and Hobbes' Line Is Still a Perfect Comic Strip Quote
articles.summary: Here's something that might win you some points in a trivia game someday: Bill Watterson named the protagonists of Calvin and Hobbes after two European philosophers. John Calvin (1509-1564) was a controversial theologian whose ideas gave rise to the predestination-oriented Calvinist branch of…
body: In general, trying to match either Calvin or Hobbes to their namesakes' philosophies doesn't work. Calvin is generally the closer of the two; as he often notes, being a young child is a sort of predestination in itself, since little of his day-to-day life is in his direct control. Hobbes, on the other hand, is a tiger, so he's largely in favor of the "nasty, brutish, and short" state of nature that Thomas Hobbes sought to avoid. If the two have anything in common, as Watterson noted, it’s that both Hobbeses don't think much of humans.

As far as the core philosophy of Calvin and Hobbes goes, Watterson provided about as close to a mission statement as you could want in a commencement speech at his alma mater, Kenyon College, in 1990.

"To invent your own life's meaning is not easy, but it's still allowed, and I think you'll be happier for the trouble," Watterson said. "Reading those turgid philosophers here in these remote stone buildings may not get you a job, but if those books have forced you to ask yourself questions about what makes life truthful, purposeful, meaningful, and redeeming, you have the Swiss Army Knife of mental tools, and it's going to come in handy all the time."

articles.title: WoW: Forever Won’t Have Dead Servers
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever will avoid repeating WoW Classic's mistakes and will have tools to prevent "dead" or "unsustainable" server rulesets, Blizzard said. In the past, various WoW Classic servers became "dead" over time, as players either stopped playing or transferred to other servers.
body: While Forever is going a different route with what are essentially mega servers tailored around specific rulesets, some players might still have anxiety when it comes to picking a ruleset that will be a healthy place to play long-term.

In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast, Blizzard said it has tools it can use if a ruleset's population becomes "unsustainable." Senior game designer Josh Greenfield gave the example of Forever's separate RP and (newly added) RP-PvP server rulesets. He said there were initially concerns about splitting up the RP community, fearing that one or both of the rulesets wouldn't be able to stand the test of time. He said Blizzard now believes "it will be fine," but does have options should the worst happen.

"If someday down the line, if something happens and one or both of those populations can't quite sustain themselves, we have options if we do need to say link up their auction houses or allow them to group for instanced content," Greenfield said.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever will avoid repeating WoW Classic's mistakes and will have tools to prevent "dead" or "unsustainable" server rulesets, Blizzard said.

articles.title: Artist With Music In GTA 6 Had No Idea About Any Of That
articles.summary: Cliff Richard is among the numerous famous artists who are lending their music to Rockstar's GTA 6, with Richard's classic tune "Devil Woman" appearing in the Netflix Extended Look. Richard, 86, didn't know about any of that, however, or that GTA 6 is a game and not a TV show.
body: Speaking to The Times ( via Dexerto ), Richard said of the partnership with Rockstar for GTA 6: "I was told this happened!" He said his nephew's sons told him about it. "They didn't realize I could sing like that," he said.
Richard was eventually made aware of GTA 6, but the singer doesn't know what that is. “The show is a game show, isn’t it, really? One of the biggest on TV?” he asked.
"Devil Woman" was originally released in 1976, so it's now 50 years old. Richard said he's pretty jazzed about the fact that young people will hear his music.
“People will no longer just say, ‘Oh, Cliff Richard is from the past,’” he said. “Because I am, but that past is what makes everything what it is today."

articles.title: Reddit will switch to a 'logged-in only experience'
articles.summary: Reddit will become a "logged-in only experience," and the company plans to move fast, beginning testing soon in regions outside the US before flipping the switch globally.
body: The popular community website—home to a great many official and unofficial gaming message boards—lost one million search engine referrals per week on average in October, CEO Steve Huffman said on an investor call today.

The culprit, of course, was AI. A Google search that once might have led someone to a 14-year-old Reddit thread containing the answer to a rare household cleaning problem is now likely to present that answer in an AI summary, no click required.
"Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the internet," Huffman said during a Q&A.

The CEO emphasized, however, that most of Reddit's revenue (over 80%) comes from logged-in and app users, and said that the company will focus on establishing the site as "a direct daily habit" that doesn't rely on search traffic.
points: Reddit will become a "logged-in only experience," and the company plans to move fast, beginning testing soon in regions outside the US before flipping the switch globally.

points: Some leaked info surrounding The Elder Scrolls 6 has popped up again, and The Verge is reporting that an official reveal could be around the corner, possibly November.
A leaked, but unverified, title was floating around not too long ago, suggesting the official name for the game is The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, and The Verge is sticking by that name.
The setting for the game is also heavily rumored to be Hammerfell.
The game debuted to the number two spot on Steam's most-played list, with around 723,000 concurrents.
videos.author: IGN

videos.title: Village in the Shade – Launch Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: Play Village in the Shade, now on Nintendo Switch 2:
body: Enjoy quiet, countryside living...as long as you follow the rules.
In this brand-new, hand-painted farming sim, you'll plant crops, customize your homestead, and meet a cast of intriguing characters—all with something to hide.
